# RocketNet roadmap

<!-- Generated from docs/roadmap.sexp by tools/roadmap/render.py. Do not edit this file: edit the data and run `make roadmap`. -->

Every feature RocketNet has, and every one still to come, by area. ✅ is done and tested on main; ❌ is not done yet; — does not apply. Items marked (later) are deliberately after the current work, by the owner's call. An area marked (next milestone) is the next milestone, by the owner's call.

## Connect handshake and security

The secure connect from STANDARD.md: netcode 1.02 rebuilt on public keys, with every refusal counted.

| feature | done |
|---|:---:|
| Public-key connect tokens: mint, verify and open in the standard's order | ✅ |
| Deterministic connect token vectors for minters in other languages | ✅ |
| 6-byte prefilter header with a per-title filter value and epoch | ✅ |
| Cookie gate: bounds, signature, expiry and address checked | ✅ |
| Cookie key rotates on its period | ✅ |
| Per-connection keys with forward secrecy, secrets wiped on every exit | ✅ |
| Sealed packets with every refusal proven | ✅ |
| Used-token history and one token, one live connection | ✅ |
| Admission hook drops a packet before any verify | ✅ |
| Cheap refusals before crypto: a full server refuses before keypair work | ✅ |
| Bounded handshake work per update | ✅ |
| Configurable half-open handshake deadline | ✅ |
| Replay window, cleared whole by a long sequence skip | ✅ |
| Replay window advances only after the connect check | ✅ |
| Hostile fragment ids cannot poison a reassembly slot | ✅ |
| Oversize datagrams are dropped, never truncated | ✅ |
| Release builds refuse development keys | ✅ |
| Release builds do not export development token minting | ✅ |
| Public API is NULL-safe at the boundary | ✅ |
| Refusal decisions agree with netcode 1.02 | ✅ |
| The token is bound at response open | ✅ |
| Development keys are off by default and warn on every start | ✅ |
| An unauthenticated reply is never larger than its request | ✅ |
| Session layer: identity auth with a backend, rolling magic, keyed filter value (later) | ❌ |
| complete | 95% |

| Payloads both ways from the connection response on | ✅ |
| Redundant disconnect burst, from the client or the server | ✅ |
| Large payloads fragmented and reassembled | ✅ |
| Fragments accepted only on a connected slot | ✅ |

| Per-packet acks with delivery notification | ✅ |
| Ack history that survives a long lossy path | ✅ |
| Frame sync: a fixed-rate server loop with priority and drop detection | ✅ |
| Counters on every path, each classified, conserved and named by a test | ✅ |

## Drivers

The server socket drivers below the transport, selected at runtime by the per-endpoint ROCKETNET_SERVER_TRANSPORT and ROCKETNET_CLIENT_TRANSPORT; the old names ROCKETNET_DRIVER, ROCKETNET_TRANSPORT, ROCKETNET_SERVER_DRIVER and ROCKETNET_CLIENT_DRIVER are refused aloud and never applied (sdk/rocketnet_config.cpp). Loopback is pin-only.

| feature | portable | gso | msgx | iocp | xdp | io_uring | loopback | rio |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Server driver | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Selectable by pin at runtime | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| complete | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% |

## Browser clients (later)

Browsers cannot open raw UDP, so a browser client reaches a RocketNet server through a WebTransport or WebRTC data channel front-end, either a relay or a second front-end in the server.

| feature | done |
|---|:---:|
| WebTransport (HTTP/3 datagrams) client and front-end | ❌ |
| WebRTC data channel client and front-end | ❌ |
| Relay or second front-end that bridges either into the UDP transport | ❌ |
| complete | 0% |

[Source data](docs/roadmap.sexp)

## Dedicated-NIC drivers (later)

These drivers are only for a deployment where a second NIC is exclusively the game server's and the main NIC carries admin traffic; RocketNet never takes over a shared NIC, which is why AF_XDP (the kernel stack keeps the NIC, the server steers only its own packets) is the driver for shared NICs.

| feature | done |
|---|:---:|
| netmap driver on FreeBSD (netmap is in the FreeBSD kernel) | ❌ |
| netmap driver on Linux, only if netmap enters the mainline kernel (today it needs an out-of-tree module and patched NIC drivers) | ❌ |
| DPDK driver | ❌ |
| complete | 0% |

[Source data](docs/roadmap.sexp)
